items.bold: IRAN IRIB TV from Qeshm Island: "Empty of vessels. All waiting for Iran's permission and IRGC approval." Total Hormuz control asserted on state television.
items.text: CBS News live (5 hours ago) confirmed: Iran's IRIB state television network broadcast a reporter from a location said to be near Iran's Qeshm Island on Saturday. The reporter told viewers: "Behind me, you can see the open waters, empty of vessels," and adding: "All vessels are waiting for Iran's permission and the approval of the IRGC Navy to pass through the Strait of Hormuz." The IRIB reporter said Iranian authorities were monitoring vessels as they wait to move through shipping lanes designated by Iranian military authorities, which pass very near islands the regime is using to impose tolls for passage. This is the most explicit assertion of total Iranian Hormuz control yet made on state television. Combined with NASA satellite fire signatures confirming the Omani lane is deserted, the IRIB broadcast is Iran publicly declaring sovereignty over the world's most critical energy chokepoint.

items.bold: CHARLES DE GAULLE AIRCRAFT CARRIER heading to southern Red Sea. Macron: "France ready to secure Hormuz." 40-nation multinational initiative.
items.text: CBS News and Fox News confirmed: The office of French President Emmanuel Macron announced the country's only aircraft carrier, the Charles de Gaulle, is heading toward the southern Red Sea ahead of a possible mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Macron's office: the move is intended to send "a signal that not only are we ready to secure the Strait of Hormuz but that we are also capable of doing so." France's defense ministry: "Since February 28, the French Armed Forces have been acting in a defensive posture. Alongside the British and their partners, they have worked on a multinational initiative — the result of ad hoc planning involving more than forty nations — aimed at contributing to the restoration of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, in coordination with coastal states." The Charles de Gaulle deployment is the most significant non-US military commitment to Hormuz reopening of the war. A French carrier group in the Red Sea approach to Hormuz changes the military balance of the reopening operation.

items.bold: IRAN LETTER: No formal acceptance as of 9:30 AM May 10. Baqaei: "still under review." Trump: "very possible we make a deal."
items.text: CBS News (5 hours ago) confirmed: Iran has yet to respond to the latest US proposal. Iranian FM spokesperson Baqaei told local media the proposal is "still being considered by Iranian leadership." Trump told reporters Saturday: "We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal." Trump also said the deal "might not happen." The dual-track signalling — positive talks + uncertainty — is consistent with Trump's negotiating pattern throughout the war. The Iran letter, if it arrives Sunday, will determine: (a) whether the Murkowski AUMF vote on Monday faces a White House that can claim progress, or (b) whether the Senate forces a formal war authorization vote that strips Trump's executive flexibility. The letter is the most consequential diplomatic document still awaited.

items.bold: MURKOWSKI AUMF MAY 11 — Senate returns TOMORROW. Most critical congressional pressure point of the war.
items.text: Multiple outlets confirmed: Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski's AUMF (Authorization for Use of Military Force) measure is due when the Senate returns from recess on May 11. If the White House cannot show a credible plan or diplomatic progress by Monday, Murkowski intends to introduce the measure — forcing a Senate vote on formally authorizing or ending the war. This removes Trump's executive flexibility: either the Senate votes to authorize the war (giving it congressional backing but also congressional oversight), or it votes to end it (forcing Trump to comply or face constitutional crisis). The Murkowski AUMF is the domestic political deadline that has been driving White House urgency on the Iran letter. If an Iran letter arrives Sunday with positive movement: Murkowski may delay the AUMF. If no letter or rejection: AUMF introduction Monday becomes near-certain.

military.t: IRAN IRIB TV from Qeshm Island: "Waters Empty. All Vessels Waiting for Iran's Permission and IRGC Approval."
military.d: CBS News live (5 hours ago) confirmed: Iran's IRIB state television broadcast a reporter from near Qeshm Island on Saturday. Reporter: "Behind me, you can see the open waters, empty of vessels. All vessels are waiting for Iran's permission and the approval of the IRGC Navy to pass through the Strait of Hormuz." IRIB said Iranian authorities were monitoring vessels as they wait to move through shipping lanes designated by Iranian military authorities, which pass very near islands being used to impose tolls. The reporter said that after President Trump "agreed to pause Project Freedom," Iranian authorities took full control of vessel management. This is Iran's most public assertion of total Hormuz sovereignty: broadcast on state television, from Qeshm Island, with empty waters visible behind the reporter. Combined with NASA satellite fire signatures confirming the Omani lane is deserted and the IRGC vetting agency formalised, this broadcast is Iran declaring Hormuz a managed Iranian waterway to its own population and to the world.

military.t: CHARLES DE GAULLE Aircraft Carrier Heading to Red Sea. Macron: "France Ready to Secure Hormuz." 40-Nation Initiative.
military.d: CBS News and Fox News confirmed: France's only aircraft carrier, the Charles de Gaulle, is heading toward the southern Red Sea ahead of a possible mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Macron's office: the move sends "a signal that not only are we ready to secure the Strait of Hormuz but that we are also capable of doing so." France's defense ministry: "Since February 28, the French Armed Forces have been acting in a defensive posture. Alongside the British and their partners, they have worked on a multinational initiative — the result of ad hoc planning involving more than forty nations — aimed at contributing to the restoration of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, in coordination with coastal states." This is the most significant non-US military commitment to Hormuz reopening of the 72-day war. A French carrier group in the Red Sea approach changes the force balance available for reopening operations — and gives the US diplomatic cover to reach a deal by presenting Iran with a multilateral, not just bilateral, coalition to contend with.

military.t: IRAN LETTER Pending as of 9:30 AM May 10. Trump: "Very Possible We Make a Deal." Baqaei: "Still Under Review."
military.d: CBS News (5 hours ago) confirmed: Iran has yet to formally respond to the latest US proposal. Iranian FM spokesperson Baqaei told local media the proposal is "still being considered by Iranian leadership" and that Iranian leadership will "later convey its response to Pakistani mediators." Trump told reporters Saturday: "We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal." Trump separately said the deal "might not happen." Iran agreed to give what has been agreed to and the war would be over per Trump, but if not, the bombing will resume at a much higher level and intensity. The letter, when it arrives, will be routed through Pakistan mediators to the US. If it contains acceptance of the nuclear moratorium framework: deal possible within 48 hours. If it contains new conditions: negotiations continue but AUMF vote becomes more likely.

military.t: MURKOWSKI AUMF MAY 11 — Senate Returns TOMORROW. Most Critical Congressional Pressure Point.
military.d: Multiple outlets confirmed: GOP Sen. Lisa Murkowski's AUMF measure is due when the Senate returns from recess on May 11. If the WH cannot show credible progress by Monday, Murkowski will introduce the measure — forcing a Senate vote on formally authorizing or ending the war. Hegseth testified that the 60-day war powers clock pauses during ceasefire — Murkowski disputes this. The AUMF introduction removes Trump's executive flexibility: Senate must vote to authorize (giving oversight) or end (forcing compliance). This domestic pressure point is the reason Trump has been pushing so hard for an Iran letter this weekend. If the Iran letter arrives Sunday with positive movement, Murkowski may delay. If no letter or rejection: AUMF introduction Monday becomes near-certain, markets would react negatively to congressional war authorization uncertainty.

assessment.body:
Sunday 9:30 AM IST. Day 72. Three forces converging on the most consequential week of the war.

IRAN'S STATE TELEVISION DECLARATION
Iran's IRIB broadcast Saturday from near Qeshm Island told the world in plain language:
• "Behind me, you can see the open waters, empty of vessels"
• "All vessels are waiting for Iran's permission and the approval of the IRGC Navy"
• Iranian authorities are monitoring vessels in IRGC-designated lanes near toll islands
This is not a claim or a threat. It is Iran broadcasting the operational reality from the chokepoint itself. Combined with NASA satellite fire signatures confirming the Omani lane is deserted, the IRGC vetting agency formalised in domestic law, and the northward rerouting map in effect: Iran has achieved what it set out to achieve. Hormuz is under Iranian management. The negotiation is about whether that management has international legitimacy.

THE CHARLES DE GAULLE DIMENSION
France's only aircraft carrier heading to the southern Red Sea changes the strategic picture:
• Macron: "not only are we ready to secure Hormuz but capable of doing so"
• 40-nation multinational initiative to restore navigation — UK, France, and partners
• A carrier group in the Red Sea approach = credible force for reopening operations
• Gives the US diplomatic cover: a multilateral coalition, not just bilateral US vs Iran
• Iran now faces not just the US Navy but a 40-nation coalition signalling intent
• This may be the external pressure that moves Khamenei's decision on the letter

THE LETTER AND THE AUMF
Two deadlines converge Sunday-Monday:
• Iran letter: Baqaei says "still under review" — expected via Pakistan mediators
• Murkowski AUMF: Senate returns Monday May 11
• If Iran letter positive and AUMF delayed: relief rally, Brent falls, Nifty surges
• If no letter and AUMF introduced: congressional war authorization debate, markets cautious
• Trump: "very good talks, very possible we make a deal" — and "might not happen"
The simultaneity of the letter and AUMF deadlines is not coincidental: Iran knows that a Senate AUMF vote removes Trump's flexibility to deal.

INDIA'S WEEK AHEAD
• Markets reopen Monday 9:15 AM IST
• Emkay: Nifty 29,000 March 2027 — 20% upside from here on war resolution
• Brent $80 in coming weeks per Emkay — India import bill saving Rs 120,000 Cr annually vs $126 peak
• Three catalysts Monday morning: Iran letter + AUMF + Charles de Gaulle
• Kharif fertiliser sourcing: non-negotiable decision this week for June planting
• India should explore engagement with 40-nation Hormuz initiative

VERDICT: Day 72 is the hinge. Iran's IRIB broadcast declares Hormuz under Iranian management. France's Charles de Gaulle heads to the Red Sea. Iran's letter is still being written. The Murkowski AUMF clock expires tomorrow. And Emkay says Nifty goes to 29,000 when this ends. The most consequential week of the 72-day West Asia War begins Monday morning at 9:15 AM IST.
